Repo: Tendril (current directory). Contest: sync identity and conflict. Main files are likely shared/src/jvmCommon/kotlin/com/tendril/app/sync/SnapshotSyncOrchestrator.kt, shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/tendril/app/sync/SnapshotRecords.kt, UnknownFieldMerge.kt, domain/PurgeRegistry.kt and data/purge/PurgedRecord.kt.
Claims from the map:
1. Every synced row carries a uid: String (UUID) alongside its local autoGenerate Long id.
2. Deletion is a deletedAt tombstone, and PurgedRecord remembers rows that were purged for good.
3. Sync is a snapshot union merge: each device writes a whole-database snapshot file to the folder and reads the others.
Claims about behaviour (verify each against the merge code; say which rule actually decides):
4. Concurrent edits to the same row on two devices: the row with the later updatedAt wins, whole-row (not per field).
5. Delete on device A, then a later edit of the same row on device B that never saw the delete: the merged row stays deleted (the tombstone wins regardless of time).
6. A tombstone is purged after some retention period; a device that was offline longer than that and still holds the live row does NOT resurrect it, because PurgedRecord blocks it.
7. A device clock that is ahead does not change which edit wins (no wall-clock comparison decides a conflict).
8. A new device with an empty database adopts every live row and every tombstone from the folder.
9. Fields the running version does not know about are kept on round-trip (UnknownFieldMerge).
note: behaviour claims are deliberately neutral guesses; refuted/partial is the useful answer

Repo: Chronicle (current directory). Contest: sync identity and conflict. Main files are likely app/src/main/kotlin/com/hazia/chronicle/backup/FolderSync.kt, core/data/src/main/kotlin/com/hazia/chronicle/core/data/sync/SyncManager.kt (importJson) and the SyncCodec.
Claims from the map:
1. Sync identity is scheduleUpdatedAtMillis plus scheduleUpdatedByDevice on reminders: a per-device stamp.
2. One file per device (chronicle-sync-<deviceId>.json), merged on app start.
Claims about behaviour (verify each against importJson and the codec; say which rule actually decides):
3. Every synced row has a globally unique id (UUID or similar), not a device-local autoincrement.
4. The merge is per field or per field group (field stamps), not whole-row.
5. Concurrent edits to the same field: the later stamp wins; ties are broken by device id.
6. Delete on device A, then a later edit on device B that never saw the delete: the later stamp wins, so the edit resurrects the row.
7. Tombstones are purged after a retention period; a stale device can then resurrect a purged row.
8. A device clock that is ahead wins every conflict it takes part in.
9. A new device with an empty database adopts every live row and every tombstone.

Repo: Mnemo (current directory). Contest: sync identity and conflict. Main files are likely app/src/main/kotlin/com/hazia/mnemo/data/sync/ReminderSyncManager.kt, SyncCoordinator.kt, data/local/Reminder.kt and data/local/SyncFileState.kt.
Claims from the map:
1. Every Reminder has a client-generated UUID id and updatedAtEpochMillis.
2. SyncFileState is a Room entity caching each sync file's last-seen lastModified.
3. Conflicts go to a conflict-resolution screen offering keep mine, take theirs, keep both.
Claims about behaviour (verify each against syncIn/resolve; say which rule actually decides):
4. One file per reminder (reminders/<uuid>.json), not one file per device.
5. Deletion travels as isArchived = true (a soft delete that doubles as the sync tombstone); isArchived also means done, or fired with nothing left.
6. A conflict is raised only when BOTH sides changed since the last sync.
7. An edit made only on the other device (local copy untouched since last sync) is adopted silently.
8. Delete on device A, then a later edit on device B: goes to the conflict screen.
9. Tombstones (archived rows) are never purged.
10. A device clock that is ahead has no effect on which side wins (a person decides every conflict).
